title: POC scoping - egress boundary & region-locking with NovaMed
next_steps: Redwood: share SOC2 + ISO docs and PrivateLink checklist
Customer: provide VPC CIDR ranges and Peering owners
Agree benchmark workload and dataset subset by 2025-10-02
action_items: Maya Patel: Send SOC2/ISO and network checklist (due: 2025-10-03)
Liam Chen: Draft benchmark plan + example load script (due: 2025-10-02)
Priya Shah: Share VPC CIDRs, account IDs and proposed subnets (due: 2025-10-01)
Jordan Kim: Identify 3 representative prompts/datasets for latency/cost tests (due: 2025-10-02)
header: Date: 2025-09-30 14:00 PT | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Carlos Reyes (NovaMed IT Dir), Anika Bose (NovaMed Security), Jordan Kim (NovaMed ML), Priya Shah (NovaMed Cloud Ops)
summary: POC scoping for private networking and strict data residency. Customer requires no egress to public internet, region-locking to eu-west-1 for PHI, and controlled PrivateLink/VPC peering. Discussed success criteria, workload sizing for benchmarks, timeline (4-week POC), and next steps (send compliance docs, share CIDRs, schedule connectivity window). Some minor transcription glitches - names/ acronyms occasionally mis-recognized.
topics: Introductions; current infra & constraints; connectivity options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink); data residency/region lock; egress gating and S3/NAT restrictions; benchmark sizing and success criteria; POC timeline and owners; security/compliance checklist; next steps and action items.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we have Liam from SE, and from NovaMed Carlos, Anika, Jordan, Priya. Uh, we'll run ~45 minutes, focus on private networking and egress controls for the POC.
[00:18] Carlos Reyes: Thanks, Maya. To start, we run a mix of PHI workloads and obviously residency is a hard requirement. We want the inference to stay in eu-west-1 and no outbound to public S3 buckets.
[00:34] Maya Patel: Totally, that's what we scoped in the email. Two main options: VPC peering cross-account vs AWS PrivateLink endpoints. Each has tradeoffs — peering gives lower latency but requires route table management; PrivateLink is more controlled but can add proxying/ENI overhead.
[00:52] Anika Bose: From security, our constraints: SOC 2 controls, we need KMS integration for any persisted artifacts, and proof that telemetry/audit logs do not cross region. Also SSO/SAML for console access.
[01:10] Liam Chen: Yep, we support customer-managed KMS and can configure audit log export to your Log Archive account via a private delivery path. We can also ensure model cache and KV stays in-region; no async replication out.
[01:28] Jordan Kim: For the benchmark, we're thinking of a mix: 1) chat-like sessions with long context (up to 8k tokens), 2) short paraphrase/embedding workloads. What's reasonable to size for POC?
[01:46] Maya Patel: Good q. For scoping we usually run two benchmarks — latency-focused and throughput-focused. Latency: 95 concurrent users, typical 300-token responses, target p50 < 80ms, p95 < 200ms. Throughput: sustained 120 requests/sec with batching to test cost/latency tradeoffs.
[02:04] Priya Shah: That p50 target seems ambitious for 8k context. Are those numbers for quantized models or fp16?
[02:20] Liam Chen: Mixed — our serving node will pick optimized kernels. For long context we'll be above those latencies; so we should define per-workload targets. Example: for 8k context p95 < 400ms could be acceptable, while short 300-token p95 < 200ms.
[02:38] Carlos Reyes: Important: zero egress to internet, and any S3 access must be VPC-only or S3 VPC endpoints in eu-west-1. No NAT gateway egress allowed.
[02:54] Anika Bose: Also need to confirm that backups / model artifacts don't automatically upload to Redwood-managed buckets outside our account unless explicitly configured.
[03:10] Liam Chen: Understood. For Private deployment we can run an agent in your VPC or do cross-account peering. If you prefer minimal changes, PrivateLink is the path where Redwood exposes an interface endpoint in your account and traffic never leaves the VPC.
[03:28] Jordan Kim: Does PrivateLink support streaming responses? We rely on streaming for progressive token display.
[03:44] Maya Patel: It does; streaming works over the PrivateLink endpoint, though there may be slight added latency due to the proxying. We'll measure that in the bench.
[04:00] Priya Shah: On routing, will we need to open up specific ports? Our security policy is strict.
[04:15] Liam Chen: Typical setup uses HTTPS over 443. We create an interface endpoint, you attach a security group that only allows traffic from your app hosts. No extra ports.
[04:31] Carlos Reyes: What about cross-account peering and route propagation? Our net team worries about broad route leaks.
[04:47] Maya Patel: With peering you control route tables — we'll ask for specific subnets and ensure routes only to the Redwood nodes. We can sign an addendum of allowed CIDRs. For the POC we can use a small set of /28s.
[05:03] Anika Bose: Auditability: we need per-request logs with user-id and model-version, kept in-region, and retention control. Can Redwood push logs to our CloudWatch/ELK over PrivateLink?
[05:21] Liam Chen: Yes, we can export logs to your account over a VPC endpoint or S3 VPC endpoint. We'll provide a delivery config and map fields. There is a small config step on both sides.
[05:37] Jordan Kim: Benchmark specifics — we'll include a representative dataset; some inputs have PII. We need assurance that raw prompts don't leave the region for any telemetry.
[05:54] Maya Patel: Agreed. POC acceptance criteria I propose: 1) All traffic remains within eu-west-1 and egress is blocked to internet, 2) Connectivity established via chosen method (PrivateLink or peering), 3) Benchmarks meet agreed latency/throughput floors, 4) Security checklist items verified (KMS, SSO, audit exports).
[06:12] Carlos Reyes: That sounds good. Timelines? We want a 4-week POC starting as soon as connectivity is set up.
[06:28] Maya Patel: Typical plan: Week 0 - network connectivity + account setup; Week 1 - baseline benchmarks (latency + throughput); Week 2 - optimization (batching, quantization recommendations); Week 3 - run full production-like workload and handover.
[06:46] Priya Shah: How long does PrivateLink provisioning take from Redwood side?
[07:02] Liam Chen: Once we have account IDs and subnets, we can provision the endpoint in 1-2 business days. Peering similarly fast but requires route table updates on your side.
[07:18] Anika Bose: Any concerns about cross-region failover? We need ability to fail to us-east-1 during outages, but data residency for PHI must remain eu-west-1. That seems conflicting.
[07:36] Maya Patel: We can support fallback for non-PHI traffic to other regions, but for PHI we'd keep active in eu-west-1. We can set routing policies to prefer eu-west-1 and only send non-sensitive traffic to fallback regions.
[07:54] Carlos Reyes: Ok. Cost side — does PrivateLink have noticeable cost delta vs peering?
[08:10] Liam Chen: PrivateLink has per-GB and endpoint-hour charges from cloud provider; peering is just cross-AZ bandwidth. We'll share a cost sensitivity table. For our Dedicated offering, network egress is minimized by design.
[08:26] Jordan Kim: Bench load script — can you provide an example that respects rate limits and uses realistic token distributions?
[08:42] Liam Chen: Yes, I'll attach our JMeter lua script and a small Go load generator. We'll parameterize token length and concurrency.
[08:58] Maya Patel: On security docs: we'll send SOC2 report redacted, penetration test summary, and a PrivateLink checklist that lists required IAM roles, subnets, and security groups.
[09:14] Anika Bose: Good. Also, any automated model update process must be controlled — we want pinned model versions during POC to avoid regressions.
[09:30] Liam Chen: You can pin model versions; rollouts are configurable with canary settings. We'll default to the pinned version for the POC.
[09:46] Priya Shah: How do you handle KV cache persistence? If the serving node keeps KV cache on local NVMe, is that encrypted?
[10:02] Liam Chen: KV cache resides in-memory and transient storage; any persisted checkpoints are encrypted using your KMS. For in-memory there's no disk snapshot unless configured.
[10:18] Jordan Kim: For throughput tests we want to try quantized model variant. Will Redwood auto-select quantization or do we need to provide model artifacts?
[10:34] Liam Chen: We can serve quantized variants if you pick a supported model. If you're using a community model we can recommend a 4-bit quant profile and test impact on accuracy.
[10:50] Carlos Reyes: Accuracy regressions are a concern — we'll run a small eval suite pre/post quant.
[11:06] Maya Patel: Great. Let's nail down acceptance numbers now so everybody's aligned. Proposed acceptance: Latency benchmark — short context (<=512 tokens): p50 < 60ms, p95 < 180ms; long context (>=4k tokens): p95 < 400ms. Throughput: sustain 120 req/s with 95% success over 10 minutes. Cost: keep per-1M tokens below a target threshold we'll exchange offline.
[11:34] Anika Bose: We need the exact schema of logs you export, include identity fields, model version, request id, and region tag.
[11:50] Liam Chen: We'll provide mapping and a sample log blob.
[12:06] Priya Shah: Network details — we will share 2 /28 subnets and the owner account id. What about DNS?
[12:22] Maya Patel: For PrivateLink we use interface endpoints and private DNS if you opt-in. If you'd rather map a CNAME to your internal FQDN, we can support that.
[12:38] Carlos Reyes: Who will run the initial bench? We prefer Redwood to run baseline then we run tuned tests.
[12:54] Liam Chen: We can run baseline and hand you the runbook so you can reproduce. For the POC we'll do 3 baseline runs and 2 tuned runs.
[13:10] Jordan Kim: A note on datasets: some examples will include PHI-like tokens; we will scrub PII where possible but it's still sensitive. Ensure logs/hot cache does not leak.
[13:26] Maya Patel: Affirmative. We'll ensure logs are filtered and only the fields you authorize are persisted.
[13:42] Maya Patel: Any blockers for starting the connectivity window?
[13:58] Priya Shah: We need the PrivateLink checklist and a contact at Redwood's network team. Also need to confirm a maintenance window for route changes.
[14:14] Maya Patel: I'll include network contacts in the doc. We prefer a 2-hour window for initial setup to validate endpoints.
[14:30] Carlos Reyes: OK. On success criteria: after the bench we want a small tech review with Redwood to review any anomalies and tuning knobs.
[14:46] Maya Patel: We'll do a mid-POC sync after the optimization week.
[15:02] Anika Bose: One more compliance item: can Redwood sign a Data Processing Addendum specifying in-region processing and not to transfer PHI?
[15:18] Maya Patel: Yes, our legal team can provide a DPA and we can add residency clauses. I'll initiate that.
[15:34] Jordan Kim: For the load shape, we'll attach peaky loads (+burst 500 rps for 30s) to test autoscaling. Redwood, can you simulate same?
[15:50] Liam Chen: Yep — we'll include burst scenarios. Our autoscaler has policies that respect your SLOs; we can limit scaling to within the Dedicated pool assigned to the POC.
[16:06] Priya Shah: Any limitations on PrivateLink across accounts in different orgs? We have some resources in a security account and some in app account.
[16:22] Liam Chen: You can centralize endpoints in a shared services account; we can route logs to a log archive account. We'll document recommended patterns.
[16:38] Carlos Reyes: Are there any IP allowlist issues? We prefer to avoid large IP ranges in the ACL.
[16:54] Maya Patel: We'll provide fixed/short CIDR ranges for the Redwood nodes used in the POC — typically small /28s.
[17:10] Anika Bose: Encryption in transit — we require TLS1.2+ and client certs for any management plane access.
[17:26] Liam Chen: Management plane can be SAML SSO and client certs for automation. Data plane is TLS enforced.
[17:42] Jordan Kim: For the evaluation metrics, we'll provide an accuracy baseline and a drift measure. If quantization degrades results over a threshold, we won't use it.
[17:58] Maya Patel: Sounds good. We'll include an eval harness as part of the benchmark repo.
[18:14] Priya Shah: Can we get an architecture diagram showing where logs and metrics flow?
[18:30] Maya Patel: Yes, Liam will attach a diagram showing PrivateLink, endpoints, log flow to your account.
[18:46] Liam Chen: I'll also put together a checklist of IAM roles we need for the export.
[19:02] Carlos Reyes: Ok next — timeline alignment. If we finalize docs by 10/3 and do connectivity 10/7, we can start baseline the week of 10/13. That fits our release window.
[19:18] Maya Patel: That's consistent with our internal ramp plan. We'll tentatively book 10/7-10/8 for connectivity.
[19:34] Anika Bose: Anything else? Procurement/legal will review DPA and run-of-scope.
[19:50] Maya Patel: I'll loop in legal and share the DPA draft.
[20:06] Jordan Kim: Small ask — can we test a sample of 10k user sessions and check KV cache behavior?
[20:22] Liam Chen: Absolutely — we'll include that in the workload matrix.
[20:38] Priya Shah: Make sure the bench scripts support replay mode so we can run against our dev env later.
[20:54] Liam Chen: We'll provide a reproducible containerized runner.
[21:10] Carlos Reyes: Sounds good. If we hit blockers, who is the escalation?
[21:26] Maya Patel: Primary Redwood contacts: Maya (AE), Liam (SE), and we have a network on-call I'll share. For urgent security matters, I'll include our security SME.
[21:42] Anika Bose: We'll circulate our internal reviewers list to ensure approvals happen fast.
[21:58] Maya Patel: Okay recap: Redwood sends SOC2/ISO, PrivateLink checklist, benchmark repo and runbook; NovaMed shares CIDRs, account IDs, dataset sample and acceptance targets; schedule connectivity 10/07.
[22:14] Carlos Reyes: Confirmed.
[22:30] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and set the calendar invite.
[22:46] (conversation wraps; several participants drop)
[23:02] [END TRANSCRIPT]
